title: Ram Murat v. State of U.P.
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to clause 6.10 representation.
headnote: Writ petition dismissed for alternative statutory remedy. The petitioner's electricity grievances may be addressed by making a representation under clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. No one appeared for the petitioner.
facts: Ram Murat filed Writ-C No. 22547 of 2020 against the State of Uttar Pradesh and two others, raising electricity-related grievances. When the Division Bench called the case, no one appeared for the petitioner. Counsel for the respondent-department was present and pointed out that the grievances could be addressed if a representation were made under clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.holding: The writ petition is dismissed on the ground of availability of alternative statutory remedy: the petitioner's grievances can be addressed by making a representation under clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
holding_units.flag: Court attributed clause 6.10 to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; catalog hit was CGRF-2007::6.10. Keyed as spoken, not corrected.

principle_tags.application: Writ dismissed because the petitioner's electricity grievances can be addressed by a representation under clause 6.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: merits of the petitioner's electricity grievances
not_decided.note: Writ dismissed solely for alternative statutory remedy under clause 6.10; the grievances were not examined.
